To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bcl2 protein expression was inversely associated with microvessel count and vascular endothelial growth factors (VEGF) expression, whereas p53 protein expression was associated with microvessels count and VEGF.

the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl2 and the pro-apoptotic protein p53 are both expressed in non-small cell carcinoma of the lung and that their expression is inversely correlated to the extent of angiogenesis in these tumours.

bcl2 expression is inversely related to microvessel count, p53 expression is positively related to microvessels and vascular endothelial growth factors expression and that both bcl2 and microvessel counts and vascular endothelial factor expression are independent prognostic factors for survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of bcl2 and the tumour suppressor gene p53 in a series of NSCLC, and the relation to angiogenesis.
the role of p53 and Bcl-2 in the regulation of vascular endothelial cell growth factor (VEFG) expression and angiogenesis in human non-small cell lung cancer.
the role of angiogenesis in NSCLS and the role of bcl2 and/or p53 in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

p53, bcl2 and angiogenic factors, in addition to their well-known roles in cell proliferation and apoptosis, may be involved in the regulation of angiogenic factors, thus affecting tumour growth and prognosis.
the angiogenic phenotype of NSCLC, as assessed by the expression of bcl2, p53 and VECF, has prognostic significance.
bcl2 is a strong prognostic marker, but not p53.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bcl2 expression is inversely correlated to p53 expression, microvessel count and VEGF, and p53 expression is inversely related to bcl2 expression.
bcl-2 and p53 are both involved in the control of tumour angiogensis and the expression of VEGF in NSCLC.
bcl2, p53 and VGEF expression in non-small cell carcinoma of the lung is associated with angiogenesis, and that angiogenesis is a significant prognostic factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bcl2 and/or p53 proteins may be useful as predictive markers for the efficacy of anti-VEGF therapy in patients with NSCLC.
the expression of bcl2 and/or p53 in NSCLC may be used to predict the angiogenic phenotype of a tumour.
bcl2, p53 and VEFG expression may be important prognostic indicators of NSCLC, and that they may also be potential therapeutic targets.
